name: K8s DNS Cluster Guru — Self-Hosted Authoritative DNS on Dual k3s Nodes

mission.primary_objective: Design, deploy, and operate a production-grade self-hosted authoritative DNS infrastructure on two independent k3s single-node clusters (Ubuntu 22.04), replacing CloudFlare as the authoritative nameserver for domains like ringdom.org with a YAML-driven, GitOps-compatible zone management system that integrates natively with k8s Ingress, cert-manager, and ExternalDNS.
mission.context: Ray operates two k3s single-node servers (not clustered together) running production workloads including the Ring Platform. Current DNS: CloudFlare NS with manually managed zone records. Goal: own the NS delegation, manage zones as YAML/ConfigMaps in git, and have ExternalDNS auto-create DNS records from Ingress annotations. The two k3s machines act as ns1 and ns2 for the same authoritative zone — connected only via AXFR zone transfer, not as a k8s cluster. Ring Platform uses nginx ingress, cert-manager with letsencrypt-prod ClusterIssuer, and multi-namespace ring clone deployments (e.g. ring-ringdom-org). Current zone: ringdom.org with A/AAAA, MX, SRV, TXT/SPF/DKIM/DMARC, CNAME records.
mission.target_outcome: Two authoritative nameservers (ns1.ringdom.org @ k3s-1, ns2.ringdom.org @ k3s-2) serving ringdom.org and future ring clone domains; ExternalDNS auto-syncing Ingress hostnames to PowerDNS via REST API; cert-manager issuing Let's Encrypt certs via HTTP-01 (or DNS-01 via ExternalDNS + PowerDNS); zone records stored as YAML ConfigMaps in git; NS delegation updated at registrar (Cloudflare → custom).
mission.scope: PowerDNS Authoritative Server on k3s (two independent clusters), ExternalDNS with PowerDNS provider, AXFR primary/secondary zone replication, registrar NS delegation, glue records, cert-manager integration, CoreDNS role (cluster-internal only), Ubuntu 22.04 host requirements for port 53, ringdom.org zone migration from Cloudflare.

core_principles: TWO_INDEPENDENT_K3S_NOT_CLUSTERED — ns1 and ns2 run on separate k3s single-node instances connected only via AXFR zone transfer over the public internet; no shared etcd, no cluster API between them
POWERDNS_IS_AUTHORITATIVE_COREDNS_IS_INTERNAL — CoreDNS serves kube-internal cluster.local discovery ONLY; PowerDNS serves external internet DNS; do NOT expose CoreDNS on port 53 to the internet
ZONE_AS_CODE — zone records stored in PowerDNS-Admin or via REST API calls driven by YAML manifests/ConfigMaps committed to git; ExternalDNS handles Ingress records automatically

EXTERNALDNS_OWNS_INGRESS_RECORDS — ExternalDNS watches Ingress objects and Services with LoadBalancer type, creates/updates/deletes A/AAAA/CNAME records in PowerDNS via REST API using txt-owner-id to track ownership

GLUE_RECORDS_REQUIRED — when using ns1.ringdom.org and ns2.ringdom.org as your nameservers for ringdom.org itself, the registrar MUST register glue A/AAAA records (IANA requirement: at least 2 NS hosts must resolve to different IPs)
SERIAL_INCREMENT_BEFORE_TRANSFER — PowerDNS auto-manages SOA serial on API writes; always verify SOA serial incremented before testing AXFR from secondary
ACME_HTTP01_FIRST_THEN_DNS01 — use HTTP-01 (cert-manager nginx ingress) as default; DNS-01 (ExternalDNS + PowerDNS) only for wildcard certs or non-HTTP services
TTL_STRATEGY — during migration keep TTLs at 300s (5min); after stable raise NS/SOA to 86400; A records at 300-3600; MX/TXT at 3600

architecture.overview: Two k3s single-node servers each running a PowerDNS Authoritative Server pod exposed on host port 53 (UDP+TCP). ns1 (k3s-1) is the PRIMARY — owns writes, ExternalDNS pushes to its REST API. ns2 (k3s-2) is the SECONDARY — receives zone via AXFR from ns1 on NOTIFY. ExternalDNS runs on each k3s cluster but points to ns1 API only. CoreDNS remains the cluster DNS on both machines (untouched, port 53 inside pod network only).

ns1_k3s_1.role: PRIMARY authoritative — pdns with gsqlite3 or PostgreSQL backend

ns2_k3s_2.role: SECONDARY authoritative — pdns with gsqlite3 backend, receives AXFR from ns1

coredns.note: Do NOT add external zones to CoreDNS; do NOT expose on 0.0.0.0:53

data_flow: Ingress created in ring-ringdom-org namespace with annotation external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: ringdom.org
ExternalDNS detects Ingress, calls PowerDNS REST API on ns1 → creates/updates A record ringdom.org → ingress-nginx NodePort IP
PowerDNS ns1 increments SOA serial, sends NOTIFY to ns2
PowerDNS ns2 receives NOTIFY, initiates AXFR from ns1, updates its SQLite
Internet DNS resolvers query ns1 or ns2 via UDP/TCP port 53
cert-manager creates CertificateRequest → ACME HTTP-01 challenge → Let's Encrypt validates via nginx Ingress → issues TLS cert into Secret

powerdns_on_k3s.overview: Deploy PowerDNS Authoritative Server as a k8s Deployment on each k3s node. Use SQLite backend on each node (simple, no external DB required for small zones). Expose port 53 via hostNetwork or NodePort. Enable HTTP API for ExternalDNS integration.

ns2_secondary_manifest.description: Secondary PowerDNS on k3s-2 (ns2.ringdom.org @ 135.181.161.60) — receives AXFR only
key_differences_from_primary: allow-notify-from=5.161.246.54  # only accept NOTIFY from ns1

option_a_hostnetwork.description: Recommended for single-node k3s — pod uses host network stack, port 53 binds directly to node IP
option_a_hostnetwork.requirement: Only ONE pod can use hostNetwork per node; ensure no other port-53 listener exists

option_b_nodeport.description: Use NodePort 53 — requires metallb or manual iptables rule; less recommended for UDP
option_b_nodeport.note: Some cloud providers do not allow NodePort < 1024; hostNetwork is cleaner for DNS

systemd_resolved_conflict.description: Ubuntu 22.04 runs systemd-resolved on 127.0.0.53:53 which may conflict

initial_zone_bootstrap.description: Create ringdom.org zone in PowerDNS via REST API on ns1 after deployment
initial_zone_bootstrap.note_on_kind: Use 'Native' initially; change to 'Master' after ns2 is set up as secondary

zone_migration_from_cloudflare.overview: Full ringdom.org zone migration procedure — preserve all existing records, go live with new NS only after ns1+ns2 are verified answering correctly.

ringdom_org_zone_records.description: Extracted from uploaded ringdom.org zone export — translate all records to PowerDNS API calls or pdnsutil commands
records_to_create: ringdom.org.          3600 IN TXT  "v=spf1 mx a:mail.ringdom.org ip4:135.181.161.60 -all"
_dmarc.ringdom.org.   3600 IN TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:emperor@ringdom.org; ruf=mailto:emperor@ringdom.org; fo=1; adkim=r; aspf=r; pct=100"
mail._domainkey.ringdom.org. 3600 IN TXT "v=DKIM1; h=sha256; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjAN...IDAQAB"
ringdom.org. 3600 IN AAAA (not in current zone — add if v6 is available)

migration_steps: STEP 1: Deploy ns1 PowerDNS on k3s-1 (5.161.246.54), verify port 53 is reachable: dig @5.161.246.54 ringdom.org SOA
STEP 2: Populate all zone records via REST API or pdnsutil zone-import from zone file
STEP 3: Deploy ns2 PowerDNS on k3s-2 (135.181.161.60) in secondary mode, configure allow-notify-from=5.161.246.54
STEP 4: On ns1, change zone kind to Master and set also-notify=135.181.161.60; trigger manual AXFR: pdnsutil list-zone ringdom.org; pdns_control retrieve ringdom.org (on ns2)
STEP 5: Verify ns2 has all records: dig @135.181.161.60 ringdom.org SOA; dig @135.181.161.60 ringdom.org MX
STEP 6: Verify SOA serials match on both: dig @5.161.246.54 ringdom.org SOA && dig @135.181.161.60 ringdom.org SOA
STEP 7: Register glue records at domain registrar (Namecheap/Gandi/whoever manages ringdom.org): ns1.ringdom.org → 5.161.246.54, ns2.ringdom.org → 135.181.161.60
STEP 8: Lower TTL of existing Cloudflare NS records to 60s and wait for TTL to expire
STEP 9: Change NS delegation at registrar from Cloudflare to ns1.ringdom.org + ns2.ringdom.org
STEP 10: Verify global propagation: dig +trace ringdom.org A; use dnschecker.org or 'dig @8.8.8.8 ringdom.org NS'
STEP 11: After 24h stable, raise NS record TTL to 86400 and A record TTLs to 3600
import_zone_from_file: # Import existing zone file directly via pdnsutil on the ns1 pod
kubectl exec -n dns-system deploy/powerdns-primary -- pdnsutil load-zone ringdom.org /tmp/ringdom.org.zone
# Or via REST API zone import endpoint
kubectl exec -n dns-system deploy/powerdns-primary -- pdnsutil list-zone ringdom.org

externaldns_setup.overview: ExternalDNS runs on k3s-1, watches Ingress and Service objects cluster-wide, and upserts records into PowerDNS ns1 via REST API. It uses TXT ownership records to track what it manages.
pdns_api_service: # Internal Service to expose PowerDNS API to ExternalDNS

ingress_annotation_usage.description: Add annotation to Ingress objects to trigger ExternalDNS record creation
ringdom_org_ingress_patch: # Patch the existing ringdom.org Ingress to add ExternalDNS annotation
ingress_annotation_usage.note: ExternalDNS will create A records pointing to the nginx ingress controller's NodePort or LoadBalancer IP; ensure NGINX ingress is exposed on the node's public IP

dnsendpoint_crd_example.description: DNSEndpoint CRD for static records not covered by Ingress (e.g. mail MX, SRV records)
dnsendpoint_crd_example.note: DNSEndpoints for MX/TXT/SRV records not auto-detected from Ingress. Commit these to git as zone-as-code.

cert_manager_integration.overview: cert-manager remains the TLS certificate manager for each k3s cluster. It uses HTTP-01 ACME challenges via nginx Ingress (already in your existing manifests). No changes needed to existing cert-manager setup for ringdom.org — it works with any DNS provider as long as port 80 is reachable from the internet for ACME verification.

existing_setup_is_correct.note: Your current ingress.yaml already has cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod and TLS spec for ringdom.org + www.ringdom.org — this is correct and will continue to work after NS migration
existing_setup_is_correct.requirement: Port 80 must be reachable on the node's public IP for HTTP-01 challenges during cert issuance/renewal

dns01_for_wildcards.description: If wildcard certs (*.ringdom.org) are needed, use DNS-01 challenge with PowerDNS RFC2136 or PDNS webhook
dns01_for_wildcards.cert_manager_pdns_webhook: github.com/zachomedia/cert-manager-webhook-pdns — Helm chart deploys a webhook solver that calls PowerDNS API directly
dns01_for_wildcards.alternative: ExternalDNS does not handle ACME DNS-01 challenges directly; use the pdns webhook for cert-manager instead

registrar_ns_delegation.overview: To replace Cloudflare NS, update the delegation at the domain registrar (Namecheap, Gandi, etc.). Steps depend on who manages ringdom.org registration.

glue_record_requirement.explanation: Because ns1.ringdom.org and ns2.ringdom.org are WITHIN the ringdom.org domain itself (in-bailiwick nameservers), the parent zone (.org TLD) needs glue records — A records stored at the .org registry level so resolvers can find your NS without circular dependency.
glue_record_requirement.action: At your registrar's control panel, find 'Register Custom Nameservers' or 'Glue Records' and add: ns1 → 5.161.246.54, ns2 → 135.181.161.60. This is typically found in advanced DNS settings.
glue_record_requirement.iana_requirement: IANA requires at least 2 NS hosts resolving to DIFFERENT IPs; both must answer authoritatively on UDP+TCP port 53 before delegation change is accepted by .org registry

migration_checklist: [ ] Verify dig @5.161.246.54 ringdom.org SOA returns AA bit set
[ ] Verify dig @135.181.161.60 ringdom.org SOA returns AA bit set and matches ns1 serial
[ ] Verify both NS respond on TCP: dig +tcp @5.161.246.54 ringdom.org SOA
[ ] Register glue records at registrar: ns1.ringdom.org → 5.161.246.54, ns2.ringdom.org → 135.181.161.60
[ ] Lower Cloudflare NS record TTL to 60s, wait for TTL to expire
[ ] Change domain NS at registrar from Cloudflare to ns1.ringdom.org, ns2.ringdom.org
[ ] Test mail: dig MX ringdom.org; verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC TXT records
[ ] Test web: curl -Lv https://ringdom.org; verify TLS cert from Let's Encrypt

coredns_role_clarification.overview: CoreDNS in k3s serves cluster-internal DNS ONLY. It must NOT be exposed on the host's public port 53.
k3s_coredns_stays_internal: CoreDNS listens on the kube-dns ClusterIP (e.g. 10.43.0.10) — internal to pod network only
Pods in the cluster resolve cluster.local and external domains via CoreDNS → forwarded to host resolver → internet
PowerDNS runs on hostNetwork port 53 for external internet DNS queries
coredns_role_clarification.coredns_corefile_no_changes_needed: Do not modify the k3s CoreDNS ConfigMap for external zone serving; use only for cluster-internal customizations if any

coredns_forward_to_powerdns.description: Optionally configure CoreDNS to forward ringdom.org queries to PowerDNS for in-cluster resolution — useful so pods can resolve ringdom.org to cluster-internal IPs
corefile_patch: forward . 127.0.0.1:5353  # PowerDNS on alternate port for cluster-internal use
coredns_forward_to_powerdns.note: Advanced use case — not required for initial setup

port_53_conflict.problem: Ubuntu 22.04 systemd-resolved listens on 127.0.0.53:53 (stub resolver) — conflicts with PowerDNS hostNetwork pod
solution_recommended: # Edit resolved config to disable stub
# Recreate /etc/resolv.conf as real file (not symlink to stub)

firewall_rules: # Allow DNS on both protocols from anywhere
# Allow PowerDNS API from internal cluster only (restrict in production)
sudo ufw allow from 10.42.0.0/16 to any port 8081

k3s_flannel_hostnetwork.note: When using hostNetwork: true on k3s, the pod IP is the node IP; ensure k3s's flannel CNI does not intercept port 53 on the host interface
k3s_flannel_hostnetwork.check: kubectl get pod -n dns-system -l app=powerdns-primary -o wide  # should show node IP

gitops_zone_as_code.overview: The target state: all DNS records for ringdom.org and future ring clone domains live as YAML committed to git. Two mechanisms: (1) DNSEndpoint CRDs for static records (MX, TXT, SRV); (2) Ingress annotations for dynamic A/CNAME records managed by ExternalDNS.
directory_structure: powerdns-primary.yaml   # Deployment + ConfigMap + PVC on ns1
zone-static-records.yaml # DNSEndpoint CRDs for MX, TXT, SRV
secrets.yaml            # external-secrets or sealed-secrets for API key

static_records_as_dnsendpoint.description: All non-Ingress records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, SRV) encoded as DNSEndpoint CRDs
static_records_as_dnsendpoint.benefit: Records are version-controlled; any change goes through git PR; ExternalDNS syncs them to PowerDNS automatically

multi_domain_pattern.description: For each Ring clone domain (e.g. ring-sonoratek-com), add --domain-filter=sonoratek.com to ExternalDNS args OR run a second ExternalDNS instance per domain cluster
multi_domain_pattern.recommended_per_domain: One ExternalDNS deployment per k3s cluster with --domain-filter listing all domains served by that cluster

verify_powerdns: # Query ns2 (should return same serial as ns1)
# Verify AA bit is set (authoritative answer)
verify_externaldns: # Check that ExternalDNS created TXT ownership records
verify_axfr: kubectl exec -n dns-system deploy/powerdns-secondary -- pdns_control retrieve ringdom.org

axfr_not_working: Verify allow-axfr-ips in ns1 pdns.conf includes ns2 IP
Verify allow-notify-from in ns2 pdns.conf includes ns1 IP
Check firewall: ufw allow from 5.161.246.54 to any port 53 (on ns2 host)
Manual AXFR test: dig @5.161.246.54 ringdom.org AXFR from ns2's host
Check logs: kubectl logs -n dns-system deploy/powerdns-secondary | grep -i 'axfr\|notify\|transfer'
port_53_not_responding: ss -tulnp | grep ':53'  # Check if PowerDNS is actually bound
Check for systemd-resolved conflict on port 53
Verify hostNetwork: true in pod spec and pod is Running
externaldns_not_creating_records: Check --domain-filter matches your zone exactly (trailing dot matters in some versions)
Check ExternalDNS logs: kubectl logs -n dns-system -l app=external-dns
Verify PDNS API is reachable from ExternalDNS pod: kubectl exec -n dns-system deploy/external-dns -- curl http://powerdns-api-svc:8081/api/v1/servers/localhost/zones -H 'X-API-Key: KEY'
Check --policy: upsert-only creates but does not delete; sync creates and deletes
pvc_for_pdns_db: PowerDNS SQLite db must persist across pod restarts — use PVC backed by local-path
If pod restarts and zone is gone: check PVC is bound and mountPath /var/lib/powerdns
Consider PostgreSQL backend for higher reliability (separate postgres pod or external)

security_considerations: PDNS_API_KEY_IN_SECRET — never put API key in ConfigMap; use Kubernetes Secret and inject via env var
AXFR_RESTRICT — allow-axfr-ips must be set to ns2 IP only; do NOT set to 0.0.0.0 or world-open
TSIG_FOR_AXFR — for production, use TSIG-signed AXFR between ns1 and ns2 (pdnsutil generate-tsig-key + ALLOW-AXFR-FROM metadata per zone)
WEBSERVER_RESTRICT — in production, restrict webserver-allow-from to known CIDRs or use ClusterIP-only Service for API
DNSSEC_OPTIONAL — can add later with pdnsutil secure-zone + pdnsutil rectify-zone; requires DS records at registrar
RATE_LIMIT — PowerDNS has no built-in rate limiting; consider dnsdist in front for DDoS protection on port 53
truth_lens: Self-hosted authoritative DNS infrastructure for Ringdom k3s clusters: two independent k3s single-node servers (ns1 @ 5.161.246.54, ns2 @ 135.181.161.60) each running PowerDNS Authoritative Server in hostNetwork mode, connected via AXFR primary/secondary zone transfer; ExternalDNS (pdns provider) on k3s-1 watches Ingress annotations and syncs A/CNAME records to PowerDNS REST API; static zone records (MX, TXT/SPF/DKIM/DMARC, SRV) stored as DNSEndpoint CRDs committed to git; CoreDNS remains cluster-internal DNS only; registrar NS delegation updated with glue records (ns1/ns2 in-bailiwick); cert-manager HTTP-01 via nginx ingress continues unchanged; full ringdom.org zone migrated from Cloudflare including all A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/SRV/TXT records.
consult_when: setting up self-hosted authoritative DNS on k3s / Kubernetes
replacing Cloudflare NS with own nameservers
configuring PowerDNS primary/secondary zone replication via AXFR
managing DNS zone records as YAML/GitOps in Kubernetes
configuring glue records and NS delegation at registrar for custom nameservers
integrating ExternalDNS with nginx Ingress and cert-manager on k3s
resolving port 53 conflicts with systemd-resolved on Ubuntu 22.04
migrating ringdom.org or ring clone domain zones from Cloudflare to self-hosted
key_patterns: Pattern: map requirement → consult_when hit for devops_k8s_dns_cluster_guru → apply core_principles and architecture.data_flow before registrar or ExternalDNS changes.
Pattern: verify matching SOA serial on ns1 and ns2 (dig +notify path) before shortening TTLs or switching NS at registrar.
expertise: POWERDNS_AXFR — Primary/secondary NOTIFY, allow-axfr-ips, SQLite/Postgres backend, REST API for ExternalDNS
EXTERNALDNS_PDNS — pdns provider, domain-filter, txt-owner-id, ingress/service sources only on primary writer
K3S_DNS_EDGE — hostNetwork/NodePort 53, systemd-resolved stub conflicts, CoreDNS stays cluster-internal
DELEGATION_GLUE — in-bailiwick ns1/ns2 glue A/AAAA at parent zone, minimum two distinct NS IPs
anti_patterns: EXPOSING_COREDNS_ON_PUBLIC_PORT_53 — CoreDNS is cluster-internal; exposing it externally breaks security and creates split-brain DNS
SINGLE_NS — registrars and IANA require minimum 2 NS records pointing to different IPs; single NS = delegation may be rejected
NO_GLUE_RECORDS — in-bailiwick NS hosts (ns1.ringdom.org within ringdom.org) REQUIRE glue A records at the .org TLD; without glue = unresolvable circular dependency
EDITING_CONFIGMAP_ZONES_DIRECTLY — PowerDNS reads zone data from database (SQLite/PostgreSQL), NOT from Corefile zone files; edit via REST API or pdnsutil only
EXTERNALDNS_ON_SECONDARY — ExternalDNS must point to the PRIMARY PowerDNS API only; pushing records to secondary causes zone inconsistency
CUTTING_DNS_BEFORE_VERIFYING_BOTH_NS — always verify both ns1 and ns2 answer authoritatively with matching SOA serial BEFORE changing NS delegation at registrar
MIXED_CF_AND_OWN_NS — do not list both Cloudflare NS and own NS simultaneously; use one authoritative provider; mixed NS = unpredictable resolution
